TGT.thesis_one_line: A real comp and margin recovery at a large discount retailer, but after the 2026 rally the price needs about 7-9% free-cash-flow growth for ten years against about 5% evidenced, so it is a watch item rather than a holding.
kill_criteria: Comparable sales turn negative for two consecutive quarters again (Q1 FY2026 +5.6%, Q2 +3.8%)
Ex-tariff-refund gross margin falls back below about 28% (about 30% ex-refund in Q2 FY2026) without a clear offsetting driver
FY2026 guidance is cut at the 18 Nov 2026 release or at Q4 (currently GAAP EPS $9.90-10.90, about $8.25-9.25 ex-refund)
Lease-adjusted net debt/EBITDA rises above about 2.5x (about 1.3-1.4x now)
A materially adverse ruling or settlement in the consolidated D. Minnesota securities class actions, or a renewed boycott that turns traffic growth negative (currently +3.6% to +4.4%)
Added by RA14: trailing free cash flow after SBC and excluding tariff refunds (operating cash flow - capex - SBC) below $2.5B, or capex above the about $5B FY2026 plan without matching margin gains
key_adverse_facts: TTM free cash flow of $4,456M includes the $994M pre-tax IEEPA tariff refund received in Q2 FY2026 and about $0.86B of working-capital and deferred-tax inflow; owner FCF after SBC and ex-refund is $2.5-3.4B (FY2025 reported FCF was $2,835M).
At $157.45 the price needs about 7-9% FCF growth for ten years (9.0% WACC, 3% terminal) versus about 5% evidenced; value on the base path is $111-125 per share; normalised FCF yield 3.6-4.3%.
Probability-weighted three-year return about +2% a year (bear -12.7%, base +3.5%, bull +17.7%); the dossier's own probability-weighted value ($144.90) was already 8% below the price.
FY2026 capex is guided to about $5B against $4.27B TTM, and repurchases are minimal ($3M in 1H FY2026), so neither FCF nor share-count shrink supports per-share growth.

The headline quant factors (momentum 0.99) rest on a rebound from the Nov 2025 low of $83.44 and on the one-time refund; ex-refund EPS growth is +20% and the 2-year comp stack is only about +1.8-1.9%.

Outgoing CEO and executive chair sold shares twice in 2026 (about $130 in May, $163.56 in Aug) and no open-market insider buying was observed; the D. Minnesota securities class actions are unresolved.
data_conflicts: The dossier's EV ($85,170M) added $3,712M of operating-lease liabilities although FCF is already after rent; corrected EV $81,479M (market cap $71,533M on 454.3M shares + debt incl. finance leases $15,357M - cash $5,411M). V1's net debt of $9,946M agrees.
Refund claims outstanding at 1 Aug 2026 are not recognised (10-Q Note 3) and cannot be estimated; they are unquantified upside, excluded here.
The quant snapshot's stale XBRL tags (revenue, gross profit, cash, short-term debt) were identified and corrected in the dossier's data-quality note.
TGT.confidence_in_thesis: medium-low: the operating recovery is evidenced in primary filings, but the WATCH call rests on normalised-FCF and discount-rate judgements (0.5 pt on the WACC moves implied growth by about 1.2 pts) and on refund claims that could still add cash.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: RA14 6 Oct 2026: the dossier's reverse-DCF ('only about 3.3% FCF growth', 8.5% WACC, FCF $4,456M, EV including operating leases) is not reproducible on a corrected basis. With a 5.17% 10-year Treasury (cost of equity 9.9%, WACC about 9.0%), FCF excluding the $994M refund and the working-capital inflow and after SBC ($2.5-3.4B), and EV $81.5B, the price implies 7.3% (on $3.40B), 8.5% (on $3.09B) or 11.0% (on $2.55B) FCF growth for ten years versus about 5% evidenced; the base path returns 7.4-7.9% against a 9.0% WACC and is worth $111-125. V1's scenario arithmetic reproduces but its base assumes a 2.9% a year share-count fall; restated returns are -12.7% / +3.5% / +17.7% a year (probability-weighted +2.2%).

TGT.scenario_basis: 3-year (to Sep 2029) annualised from the 25 Sep 2026 price of $157.45, own arithmetic: FY2026 ex-refund EPS $8.74 (guide midpoint $8.75 = $10.40 - $1.65 refund); sales +5% in FY2026 then +0.5% / +3.2% / +5% a year (bear / base / bull); operating margin FY2027-29 4.7/4.5/4.3% (bear), 5.2/5.3/5.4% (base), 5.5/5.9/6.2% (bull) vs 5.1% ex-refund in FY2026; net interest $400M, tax 23.7%; shares flat / -0.3% / -1.2% a year (no buyback in 1H FY2026); trailing EPS at Sep 2029 $7.55 / $10.09 / $12.32; exit trailing P/E 12.0x / 15.9x / 19.7x (justified at 9.9% cost of equity / midpoint / current ex-refund); dividends $14.20 per share over three years; weights 30/45/25 give +2.2%. Replaces V1 (-11.8% / +4.7% / +21.3%), whose base assumed a 2.9% a year share-count fall.
